# Cantonese TTS — complete guide for AI agents

> Cantonese is an open text-to-speech model for Cantonese (廣東話). It is a 0.6B
> "talker" distributed as GGUF files and run locally with the `ggk` or
> `gguf-core` Python package. Both ship the same engine, which serves the model
> behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: `POST /v1/audio/speech`.

This file is the full, self-contained reference. Everything an agent needs to
install the runtime, start the server and generate speech is below. No
JavaScript, login or API key is required to read it.

## Facts

- Task: text to speech. Input: text in written Cantonese (Traditional Chinese
  characters; mixed English is accepted). Output: 24 kHz mono audio.
- Capabilities: plain TTS, voice design (describe the voice in words), voice
  cloning (imitate a short reference recording).
- Model files (GGUF), all three are local files passed by path:
  - `cantonese-1.2-0.6b-q8_0.gguf` — the talker, about 0.99 GB. Required.
  - `tts-tokenizer-12hz-q8_0.gguf` — the 12 Hz speech codec, about 0.27 GB. Required.
  - `pig_cantonese_0.6b_adapter-f16.gguf` — a voice LoRA adapter, about 40 MB. Optional.
- Model files: https://huggingface.co/cantonese-dev
- Runtime: `ggk` (https://github.com/gguf-io/gk) or `gguf-core`
  (https://github.com/calcuis/gguf-core). Same engine, different command name:
  `ggk` vs `gguf`. Everything below works with either; swap the first word.
- Default server address: `http://127.0.0.1:8888`.
- One utterance is generated at a time; concurrent requests queue.

## 1. Install the runtime

Python 3.8 or newer. The install compiles the engine (CPU by default, Metal on
macOS). GPU backends are opt-in through an environment variable at install time.

```bash
pip install ggk                 # or: pip install gguf-core
GGK_CUDA=1 pip install ggk      # NVIDIA
GGK_HIP=1 pip install ggk       # AMD ROCm
GGK_VULKAN=1 pip install ggk    # Vulkan
```

On Windows cmd, set the variable first: `set GGK_CUDA=1` then `pip install ggk`.

## 2. Get the model files

Download the talker and the codec (and, optionally, the adapter) from
https://huggingface.co/cantonese-dev into one directory. The commands below
assume they are in the current directory.

## 3. Start the server

```bash
ggk server engine -- --model cantonese-1.2-0.6b-q8_0.gguf \
    --codec-model tts-tokenizer-12hz-q8_0.gguf
```

With `gguf-core` the same line starts with `gguf server engine --`.

Useful options (all optional):

| option | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--adapter <file.gguf>` | apply a voice LoRA adapter over the talker (repeatable) |
| `--host <addr>` | listen address, default `127.0.0.1`; `0.0.0.0` for every interface |
| `--port <n>` | default `8888` |
| `--api-key <key>` | require `Authorization: Bearer <key>` |
| `--alias <name>` | model id reported by `/v1/models` |
| `--voice-dir <dir>` | keep registered cloned voices on disk, one `<name>.json` each |
| `--n-gpu-layers 0` | run on the CPU only |
| `--seed <n>` | default seed of every request (42); `-1` = a new take each time |
| `--instruction "<text>"` | default voice description of every request |

The server is ready when it logs `speech endpoint: POST /v1/audio/speech`, and
`GET /health` answers `{"status":"ok"}`. The port opens only after the model
has loaded.

## 4. Generate speech

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "今日天氣好好，我哋出去行下街啦。", "voice": "A warm, low female voice, speaking slowly."}' \
  --output speech.mp3
```

The response body is the audio file itself (not JSON). Save the bytes.

Python, standard library only:

```python
import json, urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/speech",
    data=json.dumps({
        "input": "今日天氣好好，我哋出去行下街啦。",
        "voice": "A warm, low female voice, speaking slowly.",
    }).encode("utf-8"),
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
)
with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as res, open("speech.mp3", "wb") as f:
    f.write(res.read())
```

OpenAI SDK (the endpoint is OpenAI's speech API):

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1", api_key="not-needed")
with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
    model="cantonese",
    voice="A warm, low female voice, speaking slowly.",
    input="今日天氣好好，我哋出去行下街啦。",
) as response:
    response.stream_to_file("speech.mp3")
```

### Request fields — `POST /v1/audio/speech`

The body is JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`), or a `multipart/form-data`
form with the same field names when a recording is uploaded.

| field | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | string, required | the text to speak |
| `voice` | string | voice design: a description of the voice in plain words, e.g. `"A calm, deep male voice."`. Or the name of a registered cloned voice. The stock OpenAI names (`alloy`, `nova`, ...) are accepted and ignored |
| `instructions` | string | style instruction; appended to a `voice` description |
| `response_format` | string | `mp3` (default), `wav`, or `pcm` (raw 24 kHz 16-bit mono little-endian) |
| `stream` | boolean | `true` sends the audio with chunked transfer encoding while it is still being generated |
| `reference_audio` | string / file | voice cloning: a recording of the voice, WAV, MP3 or FLAC. Base64 (a `data:` URI is fine) in JSON, or a file part in a form |
| `reference_text` | string | voice cloning: the transcript of `reference_audio` |
| `seed` | integer | default 42, so the same request returns the same audio; `-1` = random |
| `language` | string | default `auto` |
| `max_duration` | number | cap in seconds, default 60 |
| `mp3_bitrate` | integer | kbps, default 64 |
| `model` | string | accepted, not checked |

Response: `200` with `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav` or `audio/pcm`.
Errors are JSON: `{"error": {"code": 400, "message": "...", "type": "invalid_request_error"}}`.
`401` = wrong or missing API key, `400` = bad request (the message says what),
`501` = an LLM endpoint was called on this TTS server.

### Voice design

Describe the voice in `voice` (or `instructions`). English descriptions work:
gender, age, pitch, pace, mood.

```json
{"input": "多謝你嘅幫忙。", "voice": "A cheerful young woman, bright and quick."}
```

### Voice cloning

Send 5 to 15 seconds of clean speech (60 s at most) as `reference_audio`.
With `reference_text` — exactly what the recording says — the clone is
in-context and follows the voice closely. Without it only a speaker embedding
is used, which is looser.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/speech \
  -F "input=<text.txt" \
  -F "reference_audio=@voice.mp3" \
  -F "reference_text=<transcript.txt" \
  --output cloned.mp3
```

(`<file` reads a field from a UTF-8 file; `@file` uploads the file.)

Register a voice once and reuse it by name:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/voices \
  -F "name=uncle" -F "reference_audio=@voice.mp3" -F "reference_text=<transcript.txt"

curl http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/audio/speech -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "你好。", "voice": "uncle"}' --output cloned.mp3
```

A voice name is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`. Registered voices live in
memory unless the server was started with `--voice-dir`.

### Other endpoints

| endpoint | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | `{"status":"ok"}` once the model is loaded. No API key needed |
| `GET /v1/models` | the model, with `meta.type = "tts"`, `meta.cloned_voices`, `meta.languages`. No API key needed |
| `GET /v1/audio/voices` | registered cloned voices |
| `POST /v1/audio/voices` | register a voice: `name`, `reference_audio`, `reference_text` (JSON or form) |
| `DELETE /v1/audio/voices/<name>` | remove a voice |

## 5. One-shot use without a server

The same package generates a file directly:

```bash
ggk -m cantonese-1.2-0.6b-q8_0.gguf --codec-model tts-tokenizer-12hz-q8_0.gguf \
    --instruction "A warm, low female voice, speaking slowly." \
    -t "今日天氣好好，我哋出去行下街啦。" -o out.mp3
```

`-o out.wav` writes WAV. `-r voice.mp3 --reference-text "..."` clones a voice.
`--seed <n>` picks the take (42 by default).

## Pitfalls

- **Send UTF-8.** On Windows, `curl.exe -d '{"input": "中文"}'` typed in cmd,
  PowerShell or Git Bash replaces Chinese characters with `?` before sending.
  Put the JSON in a UTF-8 file and use `-d @request.json`, or use `-F
  "input=<text.txt"`. The server answers `400` when the input is question
  marks only.
- **The response is binary.** Write the body to a file; do not parse it as
  JSON unless the status is not 200.
- **Start the server once and reuse it.** Loading takes a few seconds;
  requests after that only pay for generation.
- **Long text:** output is capped at `max_duration` seconds (60). Split long
  text into sentences and send them one by one.
- **Browsers:** the server sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so a web
  page can call it directly. Use `--api-key` if the port is reachable by
  anything you do not trust.

- ggk: https://github.com/gguf-io/gk
- gguf-core: https://github.com/calcuis/gguf-core
